query: What LC‑MS/MS validation criteria and SOPs are required for reliable adenosine and ligand quantification in mouse CSF and CP tissue (LOD/LOQ, linearity, matrix effects, recovery, stability, isotope calibration)?

response.query: What LC‑MS/MS validation criteria and SOPs are required for reliable adenosine and ligand quantification in mouse CSF and CP tissue (LOD/LOQ, linearity, matrix effects, recovery, stability, isotope calibration)?
response.answer: LC-MS/MS validation for adenosine and ligand quantification in mouse CSF and CP tissue requires LOD/LOQ, linearity, matrix effects, recovery, stability, and isotope calibration. Key criteria include calibration curves, precision, accuracy, and stability assessments. Use stable isotope-labeled internal standards for calibration.

results.content: Indeed, several alterations were observed in these cells in Pex11a knockout mice: (i) augmented size and number of peroxisomes and lipid droplets; (ii) increased sarcomere length; (iii) altered gene expression of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors, organellar fission machinery proteins and cardiac markers; and (iv) a lipid composition shift. By combining h-HepOrgs with portal mesenchyme and our previously published cholangiocyte organoids4-6, we generated patient-specific periportal liver assembloids that retain the histological arrangement, gene expression and cell interactions of periportal liver tissue, with cholangiocytes and mesenchyme embedded in the hepatocyte parenchyma. Here we measured the retrograde transport and metabolism of individual lipid species in mammalian cells using time-resolved fluorescence imaging of bifunctional lipid probes in combination with ultra-high-resolution mass spectrometry and mathematical modelling. Detailed characterization of protein digests by matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization (MALDI) peptide mapping, nanoelectrospray tandem mass spectrometry and MALDI-quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry revealed no evidence of protein degradation or modifications that could hamper identification of proteins in a sequence database.
